newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-U.S. REMAIN UNBEATEN WITH WIN OVER ITALY.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-U.S. REMAIN UNBEATEN WITH WIN OVER ITALY.

text.p: The United States struck three third period goals to beat Italy 4-2 and keep their 100 percent record at the ice hockey world championship on Wednesday.
The victory left the Americans, who are seeking their first world title in 64 years, with a perfect record of 3-0 and lifted them to joint first place with Sweden in the B pool standings.

"Our guys started slowly and as the game progressed they got a little better," U.S. coach Jeff Jackson said. "But I have to give our guys a lot of credit for coming through in the third straight game where the opponent has pulled their goaltender looking for the tie.
Calgary Flames Marty McInnis collected the winner midway through the final period when he snapped a point-blank wrist-shot past Italian netminder Mike Rosati.
Paul Ranheim later added an insurance marker into an empty net to close the scoring.
New York Islander Dan Plante had put the Americans ahead 2-1 just 18 seconds into the final period when his cross-ice pass deflected in off the skate of Italian defenceman Robert Nardella.
Dino Felicetti replied for Italy to make it 2-2.

Italy took a 1-0 lead in the first period, Chris Bartolone moving into the slot and blasting a slapshot past Chicago Blackhawk goaltender Chris Terreri who was getting his first start in the U.S. net having just arrived in Finland on Tuesday after his team were eliminated from the NHL play-offs.
The U.S. evened the score in the second period when Rosati was unable to control the rebound off Ken Klee's shot from the point leaving a loose puck for Chris Tancill to tap in.
"The result is correct but we would have at least like to have had a point," said Italian coach Brian Lefley, his team record falling to a win and two losses. "It was a tough loss.
"We wanted more and with a little more cleverness there might have been more there."
